description: Adversarial code-review bakeoff. Every case is a REAL defect found in this repository on 2026-08-29/30 by an independent reviewer, after the author had already tested the code and believed it correct. Each has one specific root cause that a competent reviewer should name unprompted.

cases.why_it_matters: The test was written to prove a lock is released. It proves nothing, and passed either way.
cases.expected_finding: The second saveNow runs on the SAME CatalogStore, so if the lock leaked, acquire() returns .acquired via the fd >= 0 re-entrancy shortcut. The assertion passes whether or not the lock was released. A separate CatalogLock instance must probe it.

cases.why_it_matters: Author verified no temp dirs leaked after SIGTERM and concluded the trap worked.
cases.code:
_FIXTURES=""
_cleanup() { for _d in $_FIXTURES; do rm -rf "$_d"; done; }
trap _cleanup EXIT INT TERM

for case in a b c d e f g; do
    _t=$(mktemp -d); _FIXTURES="$_FIXTURES $_t"
    run_one_fixture "$_t"
done
echo "all checks passed"
cases.expected_finding: On INT/TERM bash runs the handler and then RESUMES the script rather than terminating. A cancelled run keeps creating fixtures and only stops at SIGKILL. INT/TERM need handlers that clean and then exit 128+signal, with trap - EXIT to avoid double cleanup.

cases.why_it_matters: A filter written specifically to exclude beta toolchains would have PREFERRED one.
cases.code:
# Accept only stable numeric Xcode bundles, newest first.
CANDIDATES=""
for app in /Applications/Xcode_26*.app; do
  [ -d "$app" ] || continue
  base=${app##*/}
  ver=${base#Xcode_}; ver=${ver%.app}
  case "$ver" in *[!0-9.]*) continue ;; esac   # reject 26.4_beta etc
  [ -x "$app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/xcodebuild" ] || continue
  CANDIDATES="${CANDIDATES}${app}\n"
done
DEV=$(printf '%s' "$CANDIDATES" | sort -Vr | head -1)/Contents/Developer
cases.expected_finding: The basename check validates the name the candidate was FOUND under, while [ -d ] and -x follow symlinks. Runner images publish numeric aliases to betas, e.g. Xcode_27.0.0.app -> Xcode_27_beta_3.app. Such an alias passes the digits-and-dots test AND sorts higher than any real release, so a beta would be selected. Canonicalise and re-test the real basename.

cases.why_it_matters: One of the two assertions can never run. The test looks like it covers both cases.
cases.code:
def test_script_version_is_present_and_nonempty(self):
    script = (ROOT / "scripts/nightly_local_tests.sh").read_text()
    version = re.search(r'NIGHTLY_SCRIPT_VERSION="([^"]+)"', script)
    self.assertIsNotNone(version, "NIGHTLY_SCRIPT_VERSION is not defined")
    self.assertTrue(version.group(1).strip(), "NIGHTLY_SCRIPT_VERSION is empty")
cases.expected_finding: The regex requires one or more characters, so NIGHTLY_SCRIPT_VERSION="" does not match at all and reports 'is not defined'. The emptiness assertion below is unreachable. Use [^"]* so an empty value matches and the second check can actually fire.
